title: Decomposition mechanism of the polynitrogen N5 and N6 clusters and their ions

bond_params.description: Symmetric open-chain radical N1-N2-N3-N4-N5, C2v. Bonds: N1N2=N4N5=1.161, N2N3=N3N4=1.413 (CCSD(T)/6-31G(d)). Angles: N1N2N3=N3N4N5=137.7, N2N3N4=102.2 (row label 'N1N2N3 N3N4N5' in Table 2 denotes the two equal angles by symmetry).

species.notes: NEW species, N5 neutral radical (doublet ground/low-energy state).

species.method: UB3LYP/6-311+G(d) (UMP2/6-311+G(d) also gives bonds only, no CCSD(T) reported for this state)

bond_params.description: Second, higher-energy radical state, same atom connectivity as 2A1 but different angles; note angle value >180 (210.9) as printed -- likely a specific dihedral/reflex-angle convention used by the authors, transcribed as-is, needs care during reconstruction (may represent 360-210.9=149.1 or similar convention; verify against original before use).

species.notes: NEW species but flagged: the >180 degree angle value is unusual and should be double-checked (possible OCR/convention issue) rather than assumed to be a direct chain2d input; also higher in energy than 2A1 state (~by ~9 kJ/mol relative per text 'about 250 kJ/mol' context -- reread text for exact relative energy if needed).

species.method: CCSD(T)/6-311+G(d) (also MP2, QCISD, B3LYP with same basis reported: 1.337/1.324/1.334/1.326 A respectively)

bond_params.description: Regular pentagon (D5h), all N-N bonds equal.

species.notes: LIKELY DUPLICATE of existing 'N5-_pentagon' entry -- cross-check bond length against existing catalog value during dedup.

species.method: not reprinted here (paper references [9,10], says geometry 'warrants no further comments')
species.notes: V-shaped open form, terminal atoms point outward, ground state of N5+ (26 kJ/mol below triplet per this paper). No numeric geometry given in THIS paper -- see N5.pdf and N5+.pdf (this same archive batch) for actual numbers on this same species.

Described as 'a rather weak ion-molecule complex' -- asymmetric interaction of an N2 lone pair with one N=N bond of linear N3+. No numeric geometry given in this paper. Binding energy ~18 kJ/mol relative to N2 + triplet N3+ fragments (matches experimental 18.8 kJ/mol).

species.method: CCSD(T) (basis ~6-31G(d) based on context; B3LYP/6-311+G(d) and MP2 values also given in Figure 2)
species.source_note: Figure 2 (image), 'N6' equilibrium structure -- text: 'the N6 molecule is expected to be a planar-trans open-chain equilibrium geometry'

bond_params.description: Planar trans (centrosymmetric, C2h) open-chain diazide N6, six atoms in a chain: two terminal short N-N bonds (~1.15, N2-like), two medium bonds (~1.26), one long central single bond (~1.47, connecting the two N3-azide-like halves). CCSD(T) values (labeled (c) in Figure 2); B3LYP (a) and MP2 (b) alternatives also given: terminal 1.133/1.148, medium 1.241/1.256, central 1.454/1.442, angles 109.5/107.4 and 172.0/172.3.

species.notes: NEW, valuable, well-characterized species -- confirmed genuine minimum by harmonic frequency analysis (all real). A near-degenerate 'gauche' (C2) form also exists at MP2 level (energy difference ~0.2 kJ/mol, negligible) but no separate numeric geometry given for it in this paper. Cross-reference: N6-3N2.pdf (same batch) also reports this same trans-diazide species independently at CASPT2/DFT levels -- compare during dedup. A transition state 'N6-ts' for concerted 2N2 dissociation is also given in this paper's Figure 2 but SKIPPED here as it is explicitly a TS, not a minimum.
